es.summary: Embarazo en el que la madre, el feto o ambos tienen más riesgo de complicaciones que en un embarazo típico. Requiere controles más frecuentes y, a menudo, atención especializada.
key_points: Factores previos: HTA crónica, diabetes, enfermedad renal o tiroidea, obesidad, VIH y enfermedades autoinmunes.
Factores del embarazo actual: DMG, preeclampsia (HTAIE), embarazo múltiple, incompatibilidad Rh, placenta previa, APP, RPM o RCI.
Antecedentes: complicaciones en embarazos previos, cesárea previa y consumo de sustancias.
La edad mayor de 35 años también aumenta el riesgo.
Que sea ARO no significa que vaya a haber un problema, pero sí exige vigilancia más estrecha.

usage: Ejemplo: «Embarazo ARO por DMG y edad materna avanzada».
En muchos hospitales también nombra el servicio donde se internan estas pacientes: «trasladar a ARO».
nursing_care: Identificar los factores de riesgo desde los AGO y el primer control prenatal.
Coordinar controles y pruebas de bienestar fetal (NST, ultrasonido) según el plan.
Enseñar signos de alarma: sangrado, salida de líquido, cefalea intensa, visión borrosa, contracciones antes de tiempo o menos movimientos fetales.
Brindar apoyo emocional: el diagnóstico de ARO suele generar ansiedad.

en.summary: A pregnancy in which the mother, the fetus, or both are at higher risk for health problems than in a typical pregnancy (ARO in Spanish). It needs more frequent visits and often specialist care.
key_points: Pre-existing factors: chronic high blood pressure, diabetes, kidney or thyroid disease, obesity, HIV and autoimmune disorders.
Factors in the current pregnancy: gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, multiple pregnancy, Rh incompatibility, placenta previa, preterm labor, PROM or growth restriction.
History: a health problem in a previous pregnancy, previous cesarean and substance use during pregnancy.
Being over age 35 also raises the risk.
Having health problems doesn't mean there will be a problem during the pregnancy, but it calls for closer monitoring.

usage: Example: "ARO pregnancy due to GDM and advanced maternal age".
In many hospitals it also names the unit where these patients are admitted: "transfer to ARO".
nursing_care: Identify risk factors from the OB/GYN history and the first prenatal visit.
Coordinate visits and fetal well-being tests (NST, ultrasound) as planned.
Teach warning signs: bleeding, leaking fluid, severe headache, blurred vision, early contractions or decreased fetal movement.
Give emotional support: a high-risk diagnosis often causes anxiety.

sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Preconception Conditions Affecting Pregnancy
MedlinePlus en español: Problemas de salud durante el embarazo

summary.0.quote: A high-risk pregnancy is one in which you, your fetus, or both are at higher risk for health problems than in a typical pregnancy.

key_points.3.quote: Every pregnancy has some risk of problems, but your lifestyle, as well as factors like certain conditions and health issues, can raise that risk, such as: A health condition you had before you got pregnant A health condition you develop during pregnancy A pregnancy with more than one baby A health problem that happened during a previous pregnancy and could happen again Substance use during pregnancy Being over age 35 Any of these can affect your

key_points.4.quote: But just because you have health problems, it doesn't mean that you, or your fetus, will have a problem during the pregnancy.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Surveillance of fetal well-being is conducted via ordered ultrasound (US) with Doppler , nonstress test (NST) , and biophysical profile (BPP) .
